title: Minimum Interval Removals
statement: You are given a list of intervals, each written as [start, end] with start < end. Return the minimum number of intervals you must delete so that no two of the remaining intervals overlap. Two intervals overlap only if they share more than a single point: intervals that merely touch at an endpoint, such as [1, 2] and [2, 3], are NOT considered overlapping and may both stay. Return a single integer: the count of intervals removed. If the list is empty, or if no intervals overlap, return 0.
hints: If you must drop some intervals so the rest never overlap, it is easier to think about which ones you get to KEEP: maximize the kept set, and the removals are just the leftovers.

To keep as many non-overlapping intervals as possible, greedily prefer the interval that finishes earliest, because leaving the smallest possible endpoint behind gives later intervals the most room. Sort by end, not by start.

Sort by end ascending. Walk through tracking the end of the last kept interval; keep the current interval when its start is >= that end (touching is allowed), updating the tracked end. The answer is total count minus the number kept.
